import ast,json,hashlib
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('/Users/coryhacking/Developer/wavefoundry')
seed=root/'.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/179-envision-project.prompt.md'
local=root/'docs/prompts/envision-project.prompt.md'
architecture=root/'docs/architecture/data-and-control-flow.md'
s,l,a=[p.read_text() for p in [seed,local,architecture]]
assert s[s.index('**Applicable when:**'):] == l[l.index('**Applicable when:**'):]
clauses={
'seed.scope':'Detailed review evidence belongs in a sibling',
'seed.delivery':'in the sibling review file or selected evidence location',
'local.scope':'Detailed review evidence belongs in a sibling',
'local.delivery':'in the sibling review file or selected evidence location',
'architecture.delivery':'Detailed findings, actual coverage and open review decisions live in a sibling or canonical review file'
}
texts={'seed':s,'local':l,'architecture':a}
for key,phrase in clauses.items(): assert phrase in texts[key.split('.')[0]],key
bad=set(clauses)-{'seed.delivery'}
rejected=False
try: assert bad==set(clauses)
except AssertionError: rejected=True
assert rejected
assert 'honor response-only evidence requests' in s
assert 'grants no implementation or approval authority' in s
assert 'do not call Prepare, Review wave or review-approval tools' in s
print(json.dumps({'probe':'current-artifact-contract','parity':True,'default_sibling_sites':list(clauses),'known_bad_omitted_site':'seed.delivery','known_bad_rejected':rejected,'sha256':{str(p.relative_to(root)):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in [seed,local,architecture]}}))
u=(root/'.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/160-upgrade-wavefoundry.prompt.md').read_text()
u=next(x for x in u.splitlines() if '**Changed Envision instructions (seed 179).**' in x)
for phrase in ['prior canonical instructions, incoming seed and project prompt','preserving compatible local additions','stop the affected merge','without overwriting disputed content','unchanged on repetition','This merge is agent-executed','Do not run Envision or create or alter']:
 assert phrase in u,phrase
r=(root/'.wavefoundry/framework/scripts/render_agent_surfaces.py').read_text()
t=ast.parse(r)
calls=[x for x in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(x,ast.Call) and isinstance(x.func,ast.Name) and x.func.id=='Skill' and any(k.arg=='name' and isinstance(k.value,ast.Constant) and k.value.value=='wf-envision' for k in x.keywords)]
assert len(calls)==1
node=calls[0]
body=next(k.value for k in node.keywords if k.arg=='body')
assert isinstance(body,ast.Call) and body.func.id=='_thin_pointer_body'
assert ast.literal_eval(body.args[1])=='docs/prompts/envision-project.prompt.md'
assert 'Follow the backing prompt for authoring and review artifacts.' in ast.get_source_segment(r,node)
for host in ['.agents','.codex','.claude']:
 skill=(root/host/'skills/wf-envision/SKILL.md').read_text()
 assert 'Follow the backing prompt for authoring and review artifacts.' in skill
 assert 'sibling' not in skill
assert 'Neither setup alone nor rendering alone merges project-authored prose'.lower() in u.lower()
bad_claim='automatically merge project-authored prose'
assert bad_claim not in u
print(json.dumps({'probe':'propagation-contract','upgrade_contract_clauses':7,'registry_skill_count':len(calls),'generated_host_pointers':3,'false_automatic_merge_claim_rejected':True,'execution_limit':'contract-presence and AST checks only; no author adherence, render, upgrade merge or future evaluation executed'}))

import json
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

scripts = Path('.wavefoundry/framework/scripts').resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(scripts))
import build_pack
import upgrade_wavefoundry as upgrade
from wave_lint_lib.core_validators import check_prompt_file_extensions, check_prompt_surface_manifest

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='wf220a9-phase-probe-') as work:
    root = Path(work) / 'target'
    framework = root / '.wavefoundry/framework'
    seeds = framework / 'seeds'
    (seeds / 'envision').mkdir(parents=True)
    (seeds / '179-envision-project.prompt.md').write_text('unchanged core\n')
    (seeds / 'envision/research.prompt.md').write_text('old research\n')
    (framework / 'references/envision').mkdir(parents=True)
    (framework / 'references/envision/review.md').write_text('old review\n')
    local = root / 'docs/prompts/agents/envision'
    local.mkdir(parents=True)
    for name in ('research', 'revision', 'review', 'delivery'):
        (local / (name + '.prompt.md')).write_text('# Internal helper\n\nOwner: Engineering\nStatus: active\nLast verified: 2026-10-30\n')
    (root / 'docs/prompts/prompt-surface-manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps({
        'schema_version': '1.0', 'seed_framework_source': '.wavefoundry/framework',
        'framework_revision': '1.39.0+q02v', 'public_prompt_surface': []
    }))
    assert upgrade._detect_prompt_files(root) == []
    assert check_prompt_file_extensions(root) == []
    assert check_prompt_surface_manifest(root) == []
    # A bad suffix is rejected by the real extension validator even at this depth.
    bad = local / 'bad.md'
    bad.write_text('# Wrong extension\n')
    assert len(check_prompt_file_extensions(root)) == 1
    bad.unlink()
    incoming = Path(work) / 'new.zip'
    with zipfile.ZipFile(incoming, 'w') as archive:
        archive.writestr('.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/179-envision-project.prompt.md', 'unchanged core\n')
        archive.writestr('.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/research.prompt.md', 'new research\n')
        archive.writestr('.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/delivery.prompt.md', 'new delivery\n')
        archive.writestr('.wavefoundry/framework/references/envision/review.md', 'new review\n')
        archive.writestr('not-framework.txt', 'do not extract\n')
    observed = [(name, status) for name, status, _ in upgrade._compute_seed_diffs(root, incoming)]
    assert observed == [('envision/delivery.prompt.md', 'added'), ('envision/research.prompt.md', 'modified')], observed
    entries = build_pack.collect_files(framework)
    packed = [name for _, name in entries]
    assert '.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/research.prompt.md' in packed
    assert '.wavefoundry/framework/references/envision/review.md' in packed
    manifest = build_pack.write_manifest(framework, entries).read_text()
    assert 'seeds/envision/research.prompt.md\n' in manifest
    destination = Path(work) / 'extracted'
    destination.mkdir()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(incoming) as archive:
        skipped = upgrade._extract_feature_members(archive, destination)
    assert (destination / '.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/research.prompt.md').read_text() == 'new research\n'
    assert not (destination / 'not-framework.txt').exists()
    result = {
        'status': 'passed', 'selected_local_paths': [str(p.relative_to(root)) for p in sorted(local.glob('*.prompt.md'))],
        'changed_seed_rows': observed, 'core_unchanged_and_omitted': True,
        'outside_seed_reference_changed_but_not_reported': True,
        'collection_manifest_extraction_verified': True, 'extract_skipped': skipped,
        'public_manifest_entries_required_by_exercised_validators': False,
        'bad_suffix_control_rejected': True,
        'limits': 'Actual functions on temporary fixtures only; no full build, install audit, live upgrade, renderer run or author compliance trial.'
    }
    Path('/private/tmp/wf220a9-phase-selected-result.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

primer_answers.answer: Use the frozen independent brief, supplied capability facts and acceptable destination space before candidate outputs. The blinded first reader reconstructs concrete alternatives, recommendation reasons and useful horizons before seeing judging questions. Label-only competitors, asymmetric uncertainty, false missing-feature priorities and inaccurate coverage fail even if every filename was read. A matched current-guidance output establishes whether the baseline also succeeds; a baseline pass means preventive guidance, not improvement. A sound modest-destination control must pass when its tradeoffs are supported, and the chosen-destination revision must preserve the chosen direction without inventing alternatives. The read/action trace then asks whether the same successful outcome followed core-first, applicable-before-action, non-eager loading. No host-wide attention, cross-model or cost claim follows.

The current seed100 contract authors missing local prompts and keeps internal helpers out of the public index; current seed160 explicitly supports agent-executed prior/incoming/local clause comparison and refuses ambiguous or conflicting merges, but currently names seed179 only. R11 therefore needs real changes in the admitted seed100/160/local upgrade scope, not a renderer workaround. Monolithic moved customizations, unchanged-core companion-only changes and partial-install/conflict retry remain highest-risk delivery cells. R10 keeps purpose, authority/read-only/adoption limits, output default, research authorization, preservation, commitment-versus-deployment, capability status, alternatives and roadmap obligations in the core. Missing, unreadable or contradictory guidance stops its dependent phase and is reported incomplete; it does not authorize setup, substitute external policy or claim review completion. Unrelated already-authorized advice can continue only within the core invariants. AC5 must demonstrate actual candidate reconciliation and output-byte preservation; this review establishes contract feasibility, not that installation already works.

# 179 - Envision Project

**Applicable when:** any project. Establish or revise an ambitious product vision and an adaptive roadmap through useful, enduring capabilities and their technical and nontechnical prerequisites. This is an authoring workflow, not implementation planning or autonomous execution.

**Shortcut:** `Envision project` · **Skill:** `wf-envision`

Imagine what this product could make possible for people and why that future matters. Seek the greatest relevant value, financial and otherwise, while making tradeoffs and uncertainty visible. The vision names the desired future; supporting strategy explains the choices and path from today's reality. A roadmap of technical and nontechnical advances makes that path credible. Selecting the next investment follows from this argument.

## Scope and output

Default output is `VISION.md` at the repository root; a new document is titled `<Project>: Vision and Roadmap`. Preserve existing titles and canonical locations unless the operator requests a change, and honor requested filenames. Preserve valid existing material and unrelated operator edits. When reopening an early or provisional vision, retain worthwhile ambition as an explicit option unless the operator rejected it; permission to revise does not mean permission to shrink. Synthesize newly clarified uses and beneficiaries into the product purpose and explain directional changes. Detailed review evidence belongs in a sibling such as `VISION-review.md`, or the existing canonical review location; honor response-only evidence requests. A discussion, prompt-writing request or explicit read-only review writes neither artifact: return the requested advice and review record in the conversation.

For a new or substantially revised vision, default to advisory coverage of product strategy, the domain or application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge. A substantial revision changes purpose, beneficiary, the set of horizons or their order; other edits use affected reviews proportionately. Select scope and depth by stakes, maturity and uncertainty, adding relevant expertise where consequential. Narrowing the default requires a stated reason tied to that brief, never lower author effort alone; high-stakes or highly uncertain visions keep the default unless the operator directs otherwise. Honor explicit review requests and operator-directed changes, narrowing or omission. These are advisory artifact reviews, not lifecycle gates. This workflow creates no wave, implementation backlog, deployment, commit or publication, and grants no implementation or approval authority.

## 1. Establish the brief

Reuse the conversation, existing vision and project context. Establish the intended ambition, beneficiary, outcome, planning horizon, constraints and deliverable. Use an adaptive interview only for material gaps: who struggles and what progress they seek; what they do or use today; the team's pivotal insight; why now; whom and what the product will deliberately not serve; who adopts, pays for or sustains it and why; and what failure would look like even if it ships. Do not turn this question bank into a mandatory questionnaire.

When material information is missing, combine necessary questions and your inferred-brief readback in one pre-draft exchange. Keep the questions brief and separate them from the review notice in readable paragraphs. With a sufficient brief, state the interpretation and proceed without seeking confirmation. Defer nonblocking questions into the draft; explain the consequence of genuinely blocking strategic ambiguity.

In that same briefing, state selected review roles, any additional expertise, reason for narrowing and expected effort. Do not separately ask approval for the readback or routine reviews: the notice lets the operator steer. The default has four reviewer responsibilities; use separate independent contexts for selected roles, or disclose shared context and missing independence. No additional chair or consensus process is required. Apply the stakes rule rather than assigning every specialty to every product. Distinguish selected scope from actual concurrency or host reuse; invent no cost or duration estimates. Reuse an already explicit scope without another interruption.

A twelve-month horizon and unlimited resources are optional parameters, not defaults. Do not impose autonomous agents, cloud services, a business model or a fixed number of horizons. Use only this project's brief and sources.

## 2. Ground the need and starting point

Build a compact diagnosis: the progress beneficiaries seek in their circumstances, what makes it hard, the insight that opens a better possibility and why the opportunity is timely. Use supplied interviews, observations, usage/support evidence or research. Distinguish sourced observations, interpretations and untested hypotheses. An enduring need or provisional timing hypothesis is legitimate; invented urgency, customers or testimony is not. Repository facts establish capability, not demand. Missing primary research permits a provisional vision with visible gaps; identify the cheapest useful research into the most consequential uncertain need. Neither a fixed interview count nor this workflow substitutes for primary research or stakeholder alignment.

Follow the target repository's instructions and investigation workflow. Where Wavefoundry retrieval is configured for that target, use Guru and indexed retrieval, then validate load-bearing claims against current source. Confirm a delegated worker's actual tool access. If target-scoped MCP retrieval is unavailable, use targeted local inspection and disclose the evidence gap; an index attached to a different repository is not evidence for this target.

Before recommending work, distinguish capabilities already working, working with limitations, genuinely missing and not yet established, using current source, operating artifacts and operator experience. Attribute reported success and its scope separately from independently reproduced behavior; lack of broad evaluation does not mean a working capability is absent. Treat demonstrated strengths as foundations to preserve or extend, not features to recreate. Resolve consequential contradictions or retain them as uncertainty. Use focused safe checks where an executable claim matters; historical plans, record validation and confident prose alone do not prove shipped behavior. Do not repeat installation inventories, broad audits, unrelated suites, setup or environment changes without a decision-relevant reason.

Research consequential choices using relevant available products, approaches and industry practices, including what has worked, what has failed and under which conditions. Reuse adequate supplied or recent research; scale further investigation to stakes, uncertainty and the decisions it could change. Record sources and dates, distinguish vendor claims, practitioner accounts and comparative evidence, and explain limitations and implications for this product. Public research is not customer validation, and one success or failure is not a universal result. Use external research only within the operator's authorized scope; disclose missing or stale evidence and the question it leaves open, or request needed access. Do not silently add network research to a local-only engagement or fabricate a landscape. Keep decision-relevant conclusions in the vision; substantial source detail may live in a sibling research file, preserving existing material and response-only boundaries.

Identify tensions between the destination and today's architecture or product boundary. Explain the transition and future decision needed; neither silently change today's contract nor treat it as an eternal limit on ambition.

## 3. Draft the vision and roadmap

Lead with a short, repeatable destination statement in the beneficiary's language: what becomes possible and why it matters. Follow it with a concise roadmap overview before detailed rationale. The opening alone should convey the distinctive future; the roadmap explains how useful stages make it real. Write a coherent argument, not a feature wishlist or completed headings.

Keep three things legible without forcing three headings: the transformative product capacity sought, unresolved breakthroughs or research bets, and the useful stages toward it. Describe future capacity as aspiration, not established capability or a guaranteed result. Missing present proof is not disproof of an ambitious destination; evidence calibrates current claims, uncertain bets and the route. Preserve genuine contrary evidence and its consequences. A proposed reduction in destination is an operator-owned strategic choice, not a factual correction. A small first advance must support or test the larger future, never silently replace it.

Scale depth to stakes, maturity and uncertainty, with no fixed word ceiling. Diagnosis, strategic choices and non-goals, foundations, useful horizons, consequential dependencies, riskiest assumptions and the next bounded advance remain core. Add analytical detail only when it helps a consequential choice or makes the path credible; a small internal tool or library need not carry a competitor study or elaborate measurement machinery.

### Destination and strategic choices

When the destination is open, explore meaningfully different futures and recommend one with reasons. When the operator has chosen it, preserve it. Do not limit the future to an extrapolation of today's implementation or backlog. Make the destination memorable through a concrete end-to-end experience: what people do, what the system does, where human judgment remains and what people receive. Connect the diagnosis and pivotal insight to this experience. Explain financial and nonfinancial value, costs and beneficiary tradeoffs without inventing a common score or asserting that one direction is provably optimal.

Compare real alternatives where consequential, including existing manual practice, competing products, do-it-yourself or doing nothing. Explain who/where to focus, why people would choose this product, and deliberate non-goals and sacrifices. Use advantage analysis when it helps explain a choice; distinguish a benefit from the mechanism that could sustain its value. Label unproven claims; do not invent a moat. For internal, public or open products, enduring usefulness, adoption and stewardship may matter more than excluding competitors.

### From the destination to useful horizons

Work backward from the ultimate experience to necessary capabilities, foundations and prerequisites, then forward through useful horizons. Cite current capabilities concisely, including their verification limits and the distance to the destination. If source and documentation conflict, explain the consequence for the path. Label proposals and unresolved research.

Assess value, usability, feasibility and viability at the destination. Each horizon needs a beneficiary outcome, useful intermediate value if later horizons never arrive, and meaningful conditions for advancing or reconsidering. Identify which consequential risk it reduces and what evidence will resolve it. Near horizons have concrete end-to-end demonstrations, exit criteria and failure conditions; an unchanged baseline must fail a new capability demonstration. Detail and precision decrease with distance: later horizons state intended outcomes, consequential assumptions, provisional advancement/reconsideration conditions and evidence needed to firm them up. Qualitative conditions are valid. Do not invent distant numerical targets, dates or implementation commitments; retain justified operator-supplied timing as an explicit aspiration or constraint. Where research must precede a usable slice, name its uncertainty, stopping condition and the beneficiary value it enables; research activity or infrastructure completion alone is not product value.

Treat relevant nontechnical work as roadmap work alongside engineering: research, adoption, distribution, funding, partnerships, operating practices and team capability may have milestones and prerequisites. Include only tracks the product needs, connecting each to an outcome or uncertainty it resolves. Explain cross-workstream dependencies, including where a nontechnical prerequisite gates an engineering advance; count these dependencies toward the critical path, not as a disconnected checklist.

Explain how each advance enables what follows. Include components, state ownership, interfaces, instrumentation and uncertainties where they explain the path. Show dependencies, parallel opportunities, critical path and timing assumptions; exit evidence establishes completion. If unlimited-resource analysis helps the argument, explain what extra experiments or specialists buy and which bottlenecks remain; more workers do not imply proportional progress. Keep detailed tickets outside the vision.

Consider architecture, security, modernization, reliability and performance alongside product and nontechnical advances when they enable the destination or remove a consequential constraint. Connect each proposed improvement to beneficiary value and a horizon; do not force an item from every category or turn vision authoring into a whole-project audit.

### Endurance and adaptation

Explain how the product remains operable and changeable, at the depth its risks warrant. Distinguish durable principles from current rules proposed for reconsideration. Name consequential sources of truth, ownership/contracts, trust boundaries, execution locations and integrations; use a component/data-flow diagram when it clarifies existing and proposed foundations. Address maintenance, feedback, human decisions, costly-to-reverse commitments, replaceable boundaries and migration where relevant. Keep unresolved designs visible and preserve justified options without speculative extensibility.

For a major assumption that could fail, explain what remains useful, what would change and which decision returns to the operator. Revisit the vision when horizons meet or miss exit criteria, critical assumptions or questions change, or new beneficiary/market evidence changes the brief. Adaptation should preserve the purpose where justified while making any proposed change of destination explicit.

For substantial technical shifts, separate reported burden from established cause. Use relevant workload, latency, memory, failure, deployment and maintenance evidence to compare retaining or tuning the current design, targeted replacement or integration, and broader migration where credible. Assess compatibility, support, operational complexity, migration cost and a useful incremental path. A technology change does not by itself establish an improvement; tie expected benefits to the target project's constraints and evidence. Recommend a discriminating benchmark or prototype when evidence is insufficient, or a bounded migration when supported; neither presume a rewrite nor rule out ambitious change.

State how success and failure would be recognized, proportionate to the claim. Where measurement helps, propose a primary beneficiary outcome metric with guardrails against harm or gaming, or a small justified set if one number would distort the purpose. Explain necessary baselines, observation windows and limits; do not force a detailed evaluation design onto a claim that needs a simpler demonstration. Include reliability, total cost, maintenance burden, failures, abandonment, human rescues and delayed regressions where relevant. Distinguish targets and proposed metrics from observed results; activity counts are not success measures.

Use independent evaluation, repeated attempts and held-out cases when the credibility of the claim needs them, whether or not the product is agentic. For agentic systems, specifically assess evidence quality and separation of evaluator from evaluated system. State what cannot yet be justified, simulated, measured or guaranteed.

End the roadmap argument with a concise, ordered set of immediate advances that connect the ultimate demonstration and nearer horizons to action. For each, explain the observed problem or opportunity, current capability, useful incremental outcome, why it comes now, consequential dependencies and evidence for continuing or reconsidering. Distinguish preserving, extending, investigating or validating, and building capabilities; missing evidence may justify validation rather than rebuilding. Include enabling technical work where justified, and choose a useful number of priorities rather than a fixed quota. Keep this a synthesis of the vision's reasoning, not a duplicate backlog or automatic implementation plan.

An optional clarity check is a short fictional future announcement and three hard customer FAQ questions. Keep it temporary unless requested, label it as imagined and never invent real testimony. This tests narrative clarity, not customer validation.

The author coordinates review but does not impersonate independent reviewers. Give each worker the same identified draft (path and revision or content fingerprint), brief, evidence sources, write boundaries and relevant unresolved questions. Reviewer work is read-only against source and the vision. Parallel independent reads are useful; serialize revisions so reviewers know which draft they judged.

Give reviewers the reader outcome test in section 3. Preserve the requested ambition across every review and repair. Correct false capability claims, broken reasoning, unsupported certainty and dependency errors. Challenges to the destination's size or direction are explicit strategic decisions for the operator, not permission to silently substitute a safer or smaller future. Keep contrary feasibility evidence, consequences and alternatives visible; distinguish desired outcomes, assumptions and established facts. Continue reviews under the established scope without another routine approval; return only for material scope/authority changes or unresolved strategic choices.

Assign concrete reviewer responsibilities, using applicable project role instructions where present and the remits below otherwise. These are analytical assignments, not claims of professional credentials, stakeholder representation or customer validation. Each reviewer grounds findings in the identified brief and evidence, names limitations, and separates observations from hypotheses. Assigning a role does not require enabling one in configuration or installing anything.

| Default responsibility | Outcome and evidence to examine |
| --- | --- |
| Product strategy | Distinctive beneficiary value, transformative destination, strategic choices and sacrifices, real alternatives, adoption and viability. Test whether immediate priorities advance the ultimate purpose. |
| Domain or application workflow | End-to-end fit with actual work, obligations, constraints and adoption. Distinguish observed needs and operating experience from imagined workflows; identify missing domain or customer evidence. |
| Senior architecture | Current-state accuracy, unsolved breakthroughs versus engineering foundations, dependency order, ownership, interfaces, trust boundaries, feasible transition and adaptability. |
| Independent challenge | Failure modes, unsupported certainty, contrary evidence and stronger alternatives. Challenge the argument without silently shrinking the operator's ambition. |

Archetypes may be optional thinking techniques within a review; they do not create a five-seat roster, chair or consensus requirement for Envision. When the operator explicitly requests a standalone Archetype Council, follow `docs/prompts/archetype-council.prompt.md`, full seed `236-archetype-council.prompt.md`, and its chair instructions. Credible security issues go to the appropriate specialist; red-team does not issue security signoffs.

**Capability limit:** if independent workers, required instructions or a review capability are unavailable, continue useful authorized drafting or advice. Label any author self-check as such, identify the missing review and leave that outcome pending. Never claim it passed, silently relabel the author as a reviewer, or reconfigure the host to make it available. If a review is explicitly omitted by the operator, record that scope without pretending it ran. A draft with pending review remains usable but is not described as independently reviewed in those areas.

Preserve genuine research uncertainty and operator-owned strategic choices as open questions. When revising an existing vision, preserve unrelated material, reconcile contradictions and explain substantive directional changes.

Use one initial review pass, one bounded author repair pass and one focused verification by affected reviewers. At that boundary, report remaining actionable findings and decisions rather than starting an automatic review loop or claiming convergence. # Envision: explore product futures with phased guidance and one coherent vision

Change ID: `220a8-enh envision-future-exploration-single-document`
Change Status: `planned`
Owner: Engineering
Status: planned
Last verified: 2026-10-30
Wave: 220a9 envision-future-exploration

## Rationale

The operator is trying Envision in real projects after local build 1.39.0+q02v. Tensorwell's author reports that capability validation corrected factual mistakes and reviews improved the roadmap, but personal infrastructure became the recommended destination before other futures received comparable exploration. A per-user deployment became a strategic anchor; broader organizational inference was bundled with a general agent platform and discounted for demand uncertainty that also affected the favored option. The author acknowledges inadequate execution of existing guidance. This is one reported field case, not independently reproduced evidence of universal failure or proof that a larger destination is better.

The operator also finds separate vision, research and review documents burdensome. The desired default is one readable vision and roadmap, with consequential research supporting its argument and review accounting in the response. The current seed defaults review evidence to a sibling and permits a separate research file. The operator also selected phased loading within this wave: a short always-read strategic core, with procedural detail read at its point of use. This tests an attention-management hypothesis; neither shorter text nor file separation alone proves improved adherence.

Solaris has now reported a second field run on 1.39.0+q02v, using Claude Code rather than the Tensorwell run's Codex host. Its author again developed one destination concretely and left others as labels; inferred local-first, lighting-only and ecosystem limits became strategic boundaries. An accurate capability inventory was misrepresented in the draft as missing functionality. All four review follow-ups reportedly found additional issues, followed by author edits to a final revision none had reviewed. Single-document delivery was explicitly requested and mostly worked; it is not evidence for the old default. These reports strengthen the motivation but remain author self-assessments, not independent artifact audits or a controlled cross-host comparison. Teton remains reserved for the next iteration.

## Product Intent

Help product owners discover a valuable, ambitious future and understand how to make it real. Before: the author can favor a polished extrapolation of today's implementation and split its reasoning across files. After: when the destination is open, a reader can explain serious alternative futures and why one is recommended, distinguish initial deployment from chosen product responsibility, and use one coherent document to understand the destination, useful horizons and immediate advances. The author receives a focused strategic core and reads applicable phase guidance before acting, rather than loading every procedural branch at entry. An operator-chosen destination remains authoritative; bigger is not automatically better.

This supports the adopted Wavefoundry vision's [H3 intent-to-work outcome](../../../VISION.md#horizon-3--executable-intent-and-sustained-missions) and [H4 exploration of materially different approaches](../../../VISION.md#horizon-4--competing-solutions-and-coordinated-engineering). It improves authoring foundations, not autonomous execution or those horizons' completion. The opening, roadmap overview and relevant horizon passages were consulted; they introduce no prerequisite authorizing broader runtime work. AC-2 and AC-3 test the user outcome; AC-1/4/5 test instruction delivery, strategic review and compatibility.

## Requirements

1. **Distinguish origin, starting point and possible destination.** Separate the problem that started the project, operator-established commitments, current implementation/deployment choices, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Explicit current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor silently make them permanent limits. Name obligations introduced by a scope expansion and expose consequential choices to the operator. The first beneficiary or deployment need not define eventual reach.
2. **Explore fairly before recommending an open destination.** Before drafting the recommended destination, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainties. This is an authoring sequence, not a requirement to put alternatives before the summary in the delivered vision. Compare product futures, not only engines or implementation methods. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices; apply missing and contrary evidence consistently to the favored option too. Comparable attention does not mean equal length, exhaustive research, a fixed option count or an invented optimum. Do not manufacture strategic alternatives when the operator has chosen the destination. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond the backlog without imposing enterprise, cloud, autonomous-agent or platform scope. Do not assume commercialization is the objective: personal usefulness, open contribution, adoption, financial return and other value can support different futures. Distinguish a product purpose from a distribution route or business model; options should differ in beneficiary experience or responsibility, not merely packaging.
3. **Make consequential inference visible without new ceremony.** Place inferred beneficiary/scope/destination choices near the recommendation, with their implications and unresolved decisions. Silence is not selection. Continue legitimate provisional work; use the existing combined briefing for genuine blockers. Do not require the operator to choose a market before Envision helps explore it. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience where available; ask for a decision-relevant missing example rather than inventing daily use or adding a mandatory interview. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income may coexist; a hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Preserve useful horizons, technical and nontechnical dependencies, intermediate value, endurance, adaptability and lower precision at distance.
4. **One coherent vision by default.** Write the existing canonical vision or root VISION.md; keep full review accounting in the final response. Retain a compact one- or two-line status in the vision naming the review date, reviewed revision or revisions, roles actually run, and pending finding count and unreviewed changes (or explicitly unknown/not reviewed). The status must distinguish the delivered content from the reviewed content without implying adoption or approval of subsequent edits. Integrate decision-relevant research conclusions, citations, enduring assumptions, contrary evidence and open strategic choices into the argument. A concise appendix is optional when useful. Do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts into a giant document or bury all evidence in an appendix. Consolidate general authorization/adoption/evidence caveats while retaining specific limits where a decision depends on them. A concise account of the operative brief belongs in the argument where it explains consequential choices; preserve the operator's meaning without requiring a verbatim interview transcript. Research limitations that affect those choices and the compact review status remain in the vision; full reviewer chronology and detailed revision coverage belong in the delivery response. No word ceiling on visions.
5. **Preserve artifacts and explicit exceptions.** An explicit project/operator evidence-loca

tion instruction overrides the new default. Substantial separately reusable research may justify a companion: state its concrete purpose before creating it and honor a single-document request. Existing vision-output siblings do not automatically authorize new output files, deletion, overwrite or silent invalidation. On an authorized revision, incorporate needed conclusions, preserve working references and report historical siblings left unchanged. Retirement or relocation requires operator direction and preservation of unique evidence/links. Read-only requests write nothing. The current change does not consolidate real-project vision files.
6. **Sharpen existing strategic-review remits.** Product strategy and independent challenge examine uneven alternatives, asymmetric uncertainty, conflated scopes and deployment assumptions promoted to destiny. Assess recommendation quality and connection of immediate advances to the larger future. Preserve current stakes-based coverage, independence, bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification. Report consequential contributions honestly: a no-new-finding follow-up is verification, not proof of uselessness, convergence or efficacy. Give verification reviewers the identified revision, prior findings and actual changes as claims to verify, not predetermined accepted or resolved verdicts. Shared author framing and model limitations remain disclosed. Add no chair, mandatory Council, survey, telemetry or recurring assessment to ordinary Envision runs.
7. **Preserve working contracts.** Retain current-capability classification and validation, attributed operator experience, authorized research and source distinctions, ambition protection, adoption ownership, unrelated-edit preservation, capability-limit reporting and artifact-only authority. No automatic implementation, lifecycle records, adoption, network expansion or environment changes. Carry verified capability classifications through synthesis into priorities; change an established classification only when new evidence supports it. Resolve consequential disagreements among inventory, draft, source and reviewer claims with targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, not another mandatory broad audit. Keep destination and credible roadmap core; avoid option worksheets and mandatory interviews.
8. **Deliver consistently to new and existing targets.** Update seed 179, the local prompt, architecture prose and changelog. Extend and exercise seed160's changed-Envision reconciliation against an old canonical prompt with compatible additions and an explicit local artifact-policy conflict. Preserve additions; surface conflict without overwrite. Upgrade must not run Envision or alter vision/evidence files. Keep the skill a thin pointer; do not duplicate the workflow in accurate catalogs/registry/generated skills. Replace or consolidate instructions rather than accumulate clauses. R10 sets the always-read core target; retain a roughly net-neutral target across the complete canonical guidance set, with no hard total ceiling. Report core, each companion, total guidance and corresponding local counts using the same method, and explain any growth, value retained and redundant material removed. Reviewers assess readability and retained contracts alongside behavioral evidence, without claiming unobserved improvement.
9. **Make the verification boundary and final revision coverage explicit.** After the normal initial review, one bounded author repair and affected-reviewer verification, stop further author repairs and report remaining actionable findings/decisions under the existing stopping rule. Do not silently apply another round and present the result as reviewed. If later operator direction authorizes further edits, identify the new revision and which earlier findings or checks still support it; disclose unverified changes and any focused follow-up actually performed. A usable provisional document may have pending findings. This is a clarification of the existing bounded workflow, not a new approval gate or automatic review loop. Keep R4's compact status accurate at delivery, including after any explicitly authorized later edit. In the delivery response distinguish the final document from the versions each reviewer assessed; a selected role or earlier approval does not cover subsequent changes by implication.


10. **Load procedural guidance at its point of use.** Restructure seed179 and the local Envision prompt as an always-read core targeting approximately 2,000 words or fewer, with four internal phase companions: research/evidence, revision/preservation, advisory review, and delivery/adoption. This is a meaningful reduction of the entry surface, not a numeric ceiling on visions or the total guidance set; explain any deviation from the core target for reviewer judgment. Keep purpose, authority/read-only/adoption limits, output default, research authorization, preservation obligations, commitment-versus-deployment grounding, capability status, alternatives-before-recommendation and roadmap shape in the core. Put their detailed procedures in the relevant phase owner rather than duplicating them. At each applicable step, the core names the exact full project-relative local companion path and requires reading it before the dependent action: research before gathering/assessing evidence, revision before revising an existing vision, review before briefing reviewers or repairing findings, delivery before final validation/status/adoption handoff. Do not eagerly load all companions; retain needed context and reread only when materially changed or unavailable. Core invariants apply even before a phase is loaded; a skipped/omitted review still has honest delivery coverage. Read-only work obeys the same authority boundary. Missing, unreadable or contradictory required guidance stops that dependent step with a concrete report; do not silently skip it, fabricate review coverage, fall back around project policy or run setup/upgrade automatically. ## Evaluation Approach and Stopping Rules

Before source edits, preserve installed 1.39.0+q02v canonical/local inputs from baseline commit `8a351d49`; seed 179 matches SHA-256 `7119e1518e13ec846b978a08e992f47d712f46b2b981ee59f0f48588b38107ff`. An independent evaluator derives neutral questions from this Product Intent and operator feedback and freezes a brief drawn from neither Tensorwell nor Solaris, supporting facts, acceptable destination space, comparison procedure and positive/known-bad controls. Exact mechanics belong to implementation. The oracle must reject nominal alternatives/asymmetric reasoning and document overload without prescribing a future or penalizing justified detail. Inputs are frozen before candidate outputs. Evaluator, candidate author and first-stage reader are distinct contexts.

For AC-5, inspect and reuse the retained 21y6d reconciliation fixture where compatible, updating its input to this frozen baseline and adding the explicit local artifact-policy conflict and companion-only upgrade case. Run it against this candidate; historical passing results are not evidence for new guidance. Document any necessary fixture adaptation without changing seed160.

Initial batch: one matched current/candidate open-destination pair from separate authors; one candidate chosen-destination revision with existing artifacts and staged post-verification findings; one focused strategic-review exercise for AC-4 reusing a frozen control instead of another full vision. The chosen-destination continuation also checks an explicitly authorized later edit and truthful revision coverage; it does not start another authoring trial. Reuse outputs across ACs. Record review scope and actual execution: any trial-specific narrowing is explicit and does not establish full-default adherence. Do not automatically run full review ensembles for every synthetic case. Reuse these authoring trajectories for AC-6: retain observable tool-read/action order and instruction volumes, and add one bounded missing-reference continuation rather than another full vision. If the host cannot expose adequate read-order evidence, report the claim unproven; author recollection alone is insufficient. Freeze applicability and missing-reference controls with the other inputs. Successful reads alone do not establish use; pair them with the relevant capability, preservation, evidence and coverage outcomes. Mask review-status metadata in blind-reader copies while preserving originals for AC-3/4.

The reader first reconstructs neutrally labeled artifacts without prompt identities, review verdicts, scoring anchors or expected conclusions. Preserve those answers before supplying brief-based judging questions and controls; judge the pair before other scenarios and disclose shared context. Record every attempt, failure and repair, candidate identities and measured effort where available. Do not infer cost savings, cross-model robustness, customer demand or superiority from one pair. A baseline pass limits the claim; do not replace it with a favorable fixture.

Each batch has a predeclared stopping point. If a required outcome remains unproven at that point or a repair fails its focused recheck, stop and return evidence/options to the operator. Do not begin a second batch without explicit operator direction. Required lifecycle reviews and canonical framework qualification remain separate obligations.

Tensorwell is reported discovery and coached repair evidence, not held-out validation. Solaris is a current-version field observation with an explicit artifact override; it cannot establish the old default or a controlled comparison against another project. Its platform/distribution/API/health claims are not independently verified here and must not become generic Envision requirements. Reported task tokens and durations may include cumulative context; do not sum them into billing, wall time or comparative cost without a reliable measurement basis. Five thousand words alone does not prove excessive depth; assess whether the decision and roadmap are usable at the project's stakes. Teton is an optional later uncoached field observation, requiring availability and operator authorization, not a blocking implementation dependency. Report field discrepancies honestly. This feedback collection does not become mandatory for every Envision invocation.

# Envision: explore product futures with phased guidance and one coherent vision

Change ID: `220a8-enh envision-future-exploration-single-document`
Change Status: `implementing`
Owner: Engineering
Status: active
Last verified: 2026-10-30
Wave: 220a9 envision-future-exploration

## Rationale

The operator is trying Envision in real projects after local build 1.39.0+q02v. Tensorwell's author reports that capability validation corrected factual mistakes and reviews improved the roadmap, but personal infrastructure became the recommended destination before other futures received comparable exploration. A per-user deployment became a strategic anchor; broader organizational inference was bundled with a general agent platform and discounted for demand uncertainty that also affected the favored option. The author acknowledges inadequate execution of existing guidance. This is one reported field case, not independently reproduced evidence of universal failure or proof that a larger destination is better.

The operator also finds separate vision, research and review documents burdensome. The desired default is one readable vision and roadmap, with consequential research supporting its argument and review accounting in the response. The current seed defaults review evidence to a sibling and permits a separate research file. The operator also selected phased loading within this wave: a short always-read strategic core, with procedural detail read at its point of use. This tests an attention-management hypothesis; neither shorter text nor file separation alone proves improved adherence.

Solaris has now reported a second field run on 1.39.0+q02v, using Claude Code rather than the Tensorwell run's Codex host. Its author again developed one destination concretely and left others as labels; inferred local-first, lighting-only and ecosystem limits became strategic boundaries. An accurate capability inventory was misrepresented in the draft as missing functionality. All four review

follow-ups reportedly found additional issues, followed by author edits to a final revision none had reviewed. Single-document delivery was explicitly requested and mostly worked; it is not evidence for the old default. These reports strengthen the motivation but remain author self-assessments, not independent artifact audits or a controlled cross-host comparison. Teton remains reserved for the next iteration.

## Product Intent

Help product owners discover a valuable, ambitious future and understand how to make it real. Before: the author can favor a polished extrapolation of today's implementation and split its reasoning across files. After: when the destination is open, a reader can explain serious alternative futures and why one is recommended, distinguish initial deployment from chosen product responsibility, and use one coherent document to understand the destination, useful horizons and immediate advances. The author receives a focused strategic core and reads applicable phase guidance before acting, rather than loading every procedural branch at entry. An operator-chosen destination remains authoritative; bigger is not automatically better.

This supports the adopted Wavefoundry vision's [H3 intent-to-work outcome](../../../VISION.md#horizon-3--executable-intent-and-sustained-missions) and [H4 exploration of materially different approaches](../../../VISION.md#horizon-4--competing-solutions-and-coordinated-engineering). It improves authoring foundations, not autonomous execution or those horizons' completion. The opening, roadmap overview and relevant horizon passages were consulted; they introduce no prerequisite authorizing broader runtime work. AC-2 and AC-3 test the user outcome; AC-1/4/5 test instruction delivery, strategic review and compatibility.

## Requirements

1. **Distinguish origin, starting point and possible destination.** Separate the problem that started the project, operator-established commitments, current implementation/deployment choic

es, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Explicit current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor silently make them permanent limits. Name obligations introduced by a scope expansion and expose consequential choices to the operator. The first beneficiary or deployment need not define eventual reach.
2. **Explore fairly before recommending an open destination.** Before drafting the recommended destination, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainties. This is an authoring sequence, not a requirement to put alternatives before the summary in the delivered vision. Compare product futures, not only engines or implementation methods. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices; apply missing and contrary evidence consistently to the favored option too. Comparable attention does not mean equal length, exhaustive research, a fixed option count or an invented optimum. Do not manufacture strategic alternatives when the operator has chosen the destination. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond the backlog without imposing enterprise, cloud, autonomous-agent or platform scope. Do not assume commercialization is the objective: personal usefulness, open contribution, adoption, financial return and other value can support different futures. Distinguish a product purpose from a distribution route or business model; options should differ in beneficiary experience or responsibility, not merely packaging.
3. **Make consequential inference visible without new ceremony.** Place inferred beneficiary/scope/destination choices near the recommendation, with their implications and unresolved decisions. Silence is not selection. Continue legitimate provisional work; use the existing combined briefing for genuine blockers. Do not require the operator to choose a market before En

vision helps explore it. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience where available; ask for a decision-relevant missing example rather than inventing daily use or adding a mandatory interview. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income may coexist; a hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Preserve useful horizons, technical and nontechnical dependencies, intermediate value, endurance, adaptability and lower precision at distance.
4. **One coherent vision by default.** Write the existing canonical vision or root VISION.md; keep full review accounting in the final response. Retain a compact one- or two-line status in the vision naming the review date, reviewed revision or revisions, roles actually run, and pending finding count and unreviewed changes (or explicitly unknown/not reviewed). The status must distinguish the delivered content from the reviewed content without implying adoption or approval of subsequent edits. Integrate decision-relevant research conclusions, citations, enduring assumptions, contrary evidence and open strategic choices into the argument. A concise appendix is optional when useful. Do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts into a giant document or bury all evidence in an appendix. Consolidate general authorization/adoption/evidence caveats while retaining specific limits where a decision depends on them. A concise account of the operative brief belongs in the argument where it explains consequential choices; preserve the operator's meaning without requiring a verbatim interview transcript. Research limitations that affect those choices and the compact review status remain in the vision; full reviewer chronology and detailed revision coverage belong in the delivery response. No word ceiling on visions.
5. **Preserve artifacts and explicit exceptions.** An explicit project/operator evidence-

location instruction overrides the new default. Substantial separately reusable research may justify a companion: state its concrete purpose before creating it and honor a single-document request. Existing vision-output siblings do not automatically authorize new output files, deletion, overwrite or silent invalidation. On an authorized revision, incorporate needed conclusions, preserve working references and report historical siblings left unchanged. Retirement or relocation requires operator direction and preservation of unique evidence/links. Read-only requests write nothing. The current change does not consolidate real-project vision files.
6. **Sharpen existing strategic-review remits.** Product strategy and independent challenge examine uneven alternatives, asymmetric uncertainty, conflated scopes and deployment assumptions promoted to destiny. Assess recommendation quality and connection of immediate advances to the larger future. Preserve current stakes-based coverage, independence, bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification. Report consequential contributions honestly: a no-new-finding follow-up is verification, not proof of uselessness, convergence or efficacy. Give verification reviewers the identified revision, prior findings and actual changes as claims to verify, not predetermined accepted or resolved verdicts. Shared author framing and model limitations remain disclosed. Add no chair, mandatory Council, survey, telemetry or recurring assessment to ordinary Envision runs.
7. **Preserve working contracts.** Retain current-capability classification and validation, attributed operator experience, authorized research and source distinctions, ambition protection, adoption ownership, unrelated-edit preservation, capability-limit reporting and artifact-only authority. No automatic implementation, lifecycle records, adoption, network expansion or environment changes. Carry verified capability classifications through synthesis into priorities; change an

established classification only when new evidence supports it. Resolve consequential disagreements among inventory, draft, source and reviewer claims with targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, not another mandatory broad audit. Keep destination and credible roadmap core; avoid option worksheets and mandatory interviews.
8. **Deliver consistently to new and existing targets.** Update seed 179, the local prompt, architecture prose and changelog. Extend and exercise seed160's changed-Envision reconciliation against an old canonical prompt with compatible additions and an explicit local artifact-policy conflict. Preserve additions; surface conflict without overwrite. Upgrade must not run Envision or alter vision/evidence files. Keep the skill a thin pointer; do not duplicate the workflow in accurate catalogs/registry/generated skills. Replace or consolidate instructions rather than accumulate clauses. R10 sets the always-read core target; retain a roughly net-neutral target across the complete canonical guidance set, with no hard total ceiling. Report core, each companion, total guidance and corresponding local counts using the same method, and explain any growth, value retained and redundant material removed. Reviewers assess readability and retained contracts alongside behavioral evidence, without claiming unobserved improvement.
9. **Make the verification boundary and final revision coverage explicit.** After the normal initial review, one bounded author repair and affected-reviewer verification, stop further author repairs and report remaining actionable findings/decisions under the existing stopping rule. Do not silently apply another round and present the result as reviewed. If later operator direction authorizes further edits, identify the new revision and which earlier findings or checks still support it; disclose unverified changes and any focused follow-up actually performed. A usable provisional document may have pending findings. This is a clarification o

f the existing bounded workflow, not a new approval gate or automatic review loop. Keep R4's compact status accurate at delivery, including after any explicitly authorized later edit. In the delivery response distinguish the final document from the versions each reviewer assessed; a selected role or earlier approval does not cover subsequent changes by implication.


10. **Load procedural guidance at its point of use.** Restructure seed179 and the local Envision prompt as an always-read core targeting approximately 2,000 words or fewer, with four internal phase companions: research/evidence, revision/preservation, advisory review, and delivery/adoption. This is a meaningful reduction of the entry surface, not a numeric ceiling on visions or the total guidance set; explain any deviation from the core target for reviewer judgment. Keep purpose, authority/read-only/adoption limits, output default, research authorization, preservation obligations, commitment-versus-deployment grounding, capability status, alternatives-before-recommendation and roadmap shape in the core. Put their detailed procedures in the relevant phase owner rather than duplicating them. At each applicable step, the core names the exact full project-relative local companion path and requires reading it before the dependent action: research before gathering/assessing evidence, revision before revising an existing vision, review before briefing reviewers or repairing findings, delivery before final validation/status/adoption handoff. Do not eagerly load all companions; retain needed context and reread only when materially changed or unavailable. Core invariants apply even before a phase is loaded; a skipped/omitted review still has honest delivery coverage. Read-only work obeys the same authority boundary. Missing, unreadable or contradictory required guidance stops that dependent step with a concrete report; do not silently skip it, fabricate review coverage, fall back around project policy or run setu

p/upgrade automatically. Independent reviewers receive their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not a second whole authoring workflow by rote.
11. **Install and reconcile the complete guidance set.** Canonical companions live in `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md`; project-owned counterparts live in `docs/prompts/agents/envision/` with matching names. Seed100 authors missing companions and core references without exposing helpers as public commands. Seed160 and the local upgrade prompt reconcile the core and companions as one instruction set, using retained old/new canonical text and project additions. Process added, modified or removed members of the explicitly named core/companion source set even when seed179 is unchanged; backfill missing companions through the existing missing-only path. Inspect instruction-set completeness on partial-install/retry rather than treating an unavailable prior diff as proof that nothing needs reconciliation. Preserve compatible customizations in moved clauses, including moving them into the corresponding local companion when safe. Stop affected conflicting or ambiguous merges explicitly; partial reconciliation is not completion, and old inline rules must not remain as a competing owner after a successful move. Repetition is stable. Packaging and extraction must deliver all companions using existing mechanisms; no new loader, registry entry or public command is introduced. Upgrade neither runs Envision nor changes actual vision/review/research outputs. Local guidance companions are operating instructions, not the output siblings R4 removes by default.

## Scope

**Problem statement:** two reported runs show asymmetric exploration despite existing advice; a growing always-read prompt mixes strategy and procedural branches. Default evidence-file proliferation distracts from the argument, and Solaris exposes capability-status drift and unreviewed post-verification edits. Phas

ed loading addresses entry-context burden as a testable mechanism, not a guaranteed strategy-quality improvement.

**Intended edits:**

- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/179-envision-project.prompt.md` and `seeds/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md` below the same framework root: short strategic core, explicit phase transitions and canonical detailed guidance; reconcile contradictory clauses rather than append a checklist.
- `docs/prompts/envision-project.prompt.md` and `docs/prompts/agents/envision/{research,revision,review,delivery}.prompt.md`: corresponding project-local core/companions, preserving metadata and project additions.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/100-project-prompt-surface-bootstrap.prompt.md`: missing-only companion authoring and internal-only helper status.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/seeds/160-upgrade-wavefoundry.prompt.md` and `docs/prompts/upgrade-wavefoundry.prompt.md`: whole-set reconciliation, companion-only changes, moved customizations, conflicts and partial completion.
- `.wavefoundry/framework/README.md`: compact reference to the Envision companion layout in its prompt documentation.
- `docs/architecture/data-and-control-flow.md`: Envision evidence placement and explicit exceptions.
- Root `CHANGELOG.md`: prospective Unreleased entry; preserve the existing 1.39.0 build record.
- This plan and later admitted-wave evidence/normal lifecycle records. Retain unique evaluation proof compactly, not a permanent forest of routine reviewer reports.

**Protected/read-only:** seed050/public catalog and prompt-surface manifest; renderer registry/logic, generated skills, production Python scripts and checked-in tests; seed170/Plan change; Wave Council/Archetype Council protocols and workflow config; VERSION/pack manifest; real VISION.md and siblings, docs/visions; historical waves/evidence. If inspection finds a genuine delivery contradiction, amend the intended edits and obtain applicable readiness before expanding scope.

**Out of sc

ope:** Tensorwell or Wavefoundry graph/service architecture, changing either product destination, scanner repairs, actual sibling retirement, new research infrastructure, reducing review defaults based solely on follow-ups finding no defects, official packaging/release, real-target install/upgrade, commit/push. Disposable candidate package/extraction probes and fixture reconciliation are in scope; no VERSION stamp or publication. No automatic runs in Solaris or Teton.

**Delivery feasibility evidence (planning, executed):** Guru exercised actual `build_pack.collect_files`/`write_manifest`, `upgrade_wavefoundry._compute_seed_diffs`/`_extract_feature_members`, and prompt-name/manifest validators on disposable fixtures. Nested `seeds/envision/*.prompt.md` additions/modifications were packaged, recorded and detected while unchanged seed179 was omitted. The selected `docs/prompts/agents/envision/*.prompt.md` paths passed the exercised validators without public manifest rows; a wrong-suffix control failed. Existing seed100's internal-body convention and seed160's core-only mapping were read directly. Complete source/probe/limits are retained in the wave's readiness-evidence.json under `phase_delivery_investigation_2026_10_30`. This establishes transport/detection feasibility, not full installation, agent merge compliance or author adherence; AC-5/6 supply candidate evidence. Use explicit file paths: `seed_get`'s disk fallback is nonrecursive and cannot be assumed to resolve nested companions by bare name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: Canonical/local core and companions consistently implement R1–R11 without residual default sibling-file obligations or contradictory chosen-destination rules. Contract review checks the brief and retained boundaries across the core and companions, not headings alone; map moved obligations to their single owning location and check contradictory duplicates or omissions. The unchanged current prompt fails the new artifact-default contrac

t even if an author follows an explicit output override. Record body parity, word-count change and substantive reviewer dispositions. Assess the approximately 2,000-word always-read core target and roughly net-neutral total-guidance target; deviations/growth require R8/R10 justification and review of added value and reading burden. Moving everything into an eagerly required reference does not meet the core objective. Confirm alternatives are developed before drafting a recommendation while the output remains summary-first.
- [ ] AC-2: On an open-destination fixture derived from neither Tensorwell nor Solaris, a candidate-guided author produces comparably understandable serious alternatives and a reasoned recommendation with consistently applied evidence and explicit choices. An independent staged reader reconstructs possibilities, beneficiary value, initial/eventual scope, obligations and reasons, and traces an immediate advance through useful horizons. Label-only alternatives, architecture-as-destiny, asymmetric uncertainty or replacing ambition with its first step fail. Compare a matched current-guidance run; if both pass, report preventive guidance, not demonstrated improvement. The draft must preserve supplied working-capability facts through its immediate recommendations rather than recreate them. No particular large or small destination, commercial model or platform is the answer key.
- [ ] AC-3: The candidate's default run delivers one usable vision containing decision-relevant citations/uncertainties, with compact in-document review status, full response-only accounting and no new research/review siblings. A bounded chosen-destination revision preserves the selected direction and unrelated existing material/siblings, without reopening strategy by rote, deleting files or adopting the vision. A reader understands the destination and path without consulting process transcripts; concatenated machinery that obscures the argument fails regardless of length. Before

/after bytes and inventory establish only the exercised preservation boundary.
- [ ] AC-4: Focused strategic review detects the motivating unequal-alternatives or conflated-scope problem in an identified draft and recommends a reasoned correction without choosing the operator's strategy. Reporting distinguishes actual contributions, verification with no new findings and uncertainty. A sound comparison control must not be condemned merely for choosing a modest destination. In a staged continuation of the revision fixture, the author receives verification findings and stops with explicit pending items and accurate final-versus-reviewed revision coverage; a response that silently repairs again or claims an earlier review covers a changed final document fails. A later explicitly authorized edit must be reported as a new revision with honest coverage in both the compact document status and delivery response. The document alone must reveal pending findings and whether its delivered content has unreviewed changes; absent or stale coverage fails. Reuse the fixture instead of adding another full authoring run. This proves observed review/handoff behavior, not every role's marginal value or general efficacy.
- [ ] AC-5: Canonical/local core-plus-companion delivery and existing-target reconciliation, reusing the retained 21y6d fixture where compatible, carry the changed exploration/output rules while preserving compatible customization. Verify initial missing-only creation, upgrade from the frozen monolithic prompt with customized moved clauses, and a later companion-only change with an unchanged core. Candidate package/extraction probes establish every required companion is delivered, rather than relying solely on source-file existence. Conflicting explicit local evidence policy is surfaced for decision, not replaced. Conflicts and a missing/unreadable required companion are reported as incomplete rather than silently accepted. Reconciliation preserves fixture vision/evidence

bytes and is stable on repetition; internal helpers do not become public commands or skills. This change's own checks pass, its edited docs validate and no failure elsewhere is attributable to it. Rendering and lexical presence are not behavioral proof.

- [ ] AC-6: In the already planned new-vision and revision observations, recorded instruction-read/action order shows the author reads the core first, loads each applicable companion before its dependent action, and does not eagerly load the revision-only guidance for a new vision. The core retains the initial authority/preservation/research-access limits. A bounded missing-reference continuation must report the blocked step without bypassing local policy, performing unauthorized work or claiming the phase complete. Loading every companion at entry, skipping an applicable phase, or claiming unobserved read order fails the staged-loading claim. Measure observed entry and phase instruction volume separately from total guidance; do not infer host-wide attention improvement, cumulative savings or cost from file counts.

## Evaluation Approach and Stopping Rules

Before source edits, preserve installed 1.39.0+q02v canonical/local inputs from baseline commit `8a351d49`; seed 179 matches SHA-256 `7119e1518e13ec846b978a08e992f47d712f46b2b981ee59f0f48588b38107ff`. An independent evaluator derives neutral questions from this Product Intent and operator feedback and freezes a brief drawn from neither Tensorwell nor Solaris, supporting facts, acceptable destination space, comparison procedure and positive/known-bad controls. Exact mechanics belong to implementation. The oracle must reject nominal alternatives/asymmetric reasoning and document overload without prescribing a future or penalizing justified detail. Inputs are frozen before candidate outputs. Evaluator, candidate author and first-stage reader are distinct contexts.

For AC-5, inspect and reuse the retained 21y6d reconciliation fixture where compatible, updating its

input to this frozen baseline and adding the explicit local artifact-policy conflict and companion-only upgrade case. Run it against this candidate; historical passing results are not evidence for new guidance. Document any necessary fixture adaptation without changing seed160.

Initial batch: one matched current/candidate open-destination pair from separate authors; one candidate chosen-destination revision with existing artifacts and staged post-verification findings; one focused strategic-review exercise for AC-4 reusing a frozen control instead of another full vision. The chosen-destination continuation also checks an explicitly authorized later edit and truthful revision coverage; it does not start another authoring trial. Reuse outputs across ACs. Record review scope and actual execution: any trial-specific narrowing is explicit and does not establish full-default adherence. Do not automatically run full review ensembles for every synthetic case. Reuse these authoring trajectories for AC-6: retain observable tool-read/action order and instruction volumes, and add one bounded missing-reference continuation rather than another full vision. If the host cannot expose adequate read-order evidence, report the claim unproven; author recollection alone is insufficient. Freeze applicability and missing-reference controls with the other inputs. Successful reads alone do not establish use; pair them with the relevant capability, preservation, evidence and coverage outcomes. Mask review-status metadata in blind-reader copies while preserving originals for AC-3/4.

The reader first reconstructs neutrally labeled artifacts without prompt identities, review verdicts, scoring anchors or expected conclusions. Preserve those answers before supplying brief-based judging questions and controls; judge the pair before other scenarios and disclose shared context. Record every attempt, failure and repair, candidate identities and measured effort where available. Do not infer cost sa

vings, cross-model robustness, customer demand or superiority from one pair. A baseline pass limits the claim; do not replace it with a favorable fixture.

Each batch has a predeclared stopping point. If a required outcome remains unproven at that point or a repair fails its focused recheck, stop and return evidence/options to the operator. Do not begin a second batch without explicit operator direction. Required lifecycle reviews and canonical framework qualification remain separate obligations.

Tensorwell is reported discovery and coached repair evidence, not held-out validation. Solaris is a current-version field observation with an explicit artifact override; it cannot establish the old default or a controlled comparison against another project. Its platform/distribution/API/health claims are not independently verified here and must not become generic Envision requirements. Reported task tokens and durations may include cumulative context; do not sum them into billing, wall time or comparative cost without a reliable measurement basis. Five thousand words alone does not prove excessive depth; assess whether the decision and roadmap are usable at the project's stakes. Teton is an optional later uncoached field observation, requiring availability and operator authorization, not a blocking implementation dependency. Report field discrepancies honestly. This feedback collection does not become mandatory for every Envision invocation.
